class: A tracker that opens a new authenticated database connection per method call, so one page pays a dozen handshakes
fix: PostgresTracker._connect keeps one connection per thread per DSN and reuses it; SQL errors roll back and keep it, connection failures drop it so the next use reconnects (one call fails after a server restart, not every call after it). Covered with fake-connection unit tests that need no live server.
prevention: Database-owning classes reuse a thread-kept connection and prove the reuse, drop, and thread-isolation behavior with fakes.
root_cause: Every PostgresTracker method opened, authenticated and closed its own psycopg connection; a dashboard page listing applications, documents, answers and events paid 10+ Docker-Postgres handshakes with no pooling anywhere.
symptom: Dashboard pages were slow against Postgres: each tracker call paid a full connection handshake, multiplying across every list, document, answer and event read on the page.
why_tests_missed: Database tests used a live server and asserted rows, never connection counts; nothing observed how many handshakes one page caused.
